stem: Two containers receive the same irrigation volume, but the finer-textured medium remains saturated much longer than the coarser mix. Which interpretation is most defensible?
choices: The finer medium likely has a different pore-size distribution and water/air balance that changes drainage and oxygen availability.
The finer medium likely has a lower nutrient concentration, causing slower water use even though its physical structure is otherwise comparable.
The equal irrigation volume should produce similar root-zone aeration, so the observed difference is more likely due to plant genetics than media properties.
The coarser medium likely retains more plant-available water because its larger particles create more total pore volume around the roots.
rationale: Media physical properties and pore-size distribution influence water retention, drainage, and air-filled porosity; equal irrigation volume does not create equal root-zone conditions.
